# v3.15.2 dependency security remediation

Date: 2026-10-05. Branch: `release/ima_op`.

The user required fixing the audit findings before publication. No advisory
exception, target exclusion, or severity downgrade is used.

| Finding | Remediation |
| --- | --- |
| `rustls` 0.23.42, RUSTSEC-2026-0285 | Locked to patched 0.23.45; `rustls-webpki` 0.103.15 |
| Five unmaintained `unic-*` crates | Tauri 2.12.1 / tauri-utils 2.10.1 selects urlpattern 0.6.0, removing them |
| Unmaintained `proc-macro-error` 1.0.4 | Backport upstream syn diagnostics in GTK/GLib macro crates; dependency and attr companion removed |

`rust-version` is now 1.90, matching the updated Tauri minimum. Use the checked-in
Cargo lockfile on both platforms. The vendor patches retain original licensing
and source provenance; see `vendor/README.md`. License checking includes the
local third-party crates. Release branches now run desktop CI and dependency
audits, plus native Linux tests for the backported macro crates.

Local Windows validation:

- Whole-lock `cargo-deny 0.20.2 check advisories`: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- Production `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`: **0 vulnerabilities**.
- Rust application tests: **187 passed, 5 opt-in tests ignored**.
- Frontend: build passed; **107 tests passed**.
- Macro diagnostic and existing pure unit tests: **9 passed**.
- Application rustfmt and Clippy with `-D warnings`: passed.
- Dependency licenses: **295 npm packages / 541 Rust crates** passed.

The provider/model/Agent business code is unchanged. The Tauri runtime and TLS
libraries have changed; automated tests are not a guarantee of compatibility in
every installed environment.

Validation of product source `9d8951edac09d00e004e721446630f8da04fbf4f`:

- [Desktop CI](https://github.com/atswitch/at-switch/actions/runs/37258325461):
  Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, and Linux GTK macro regression jobs succeeded.
- [Dependency audit](https://github.com/atswitch/at-switch/actions/runs/37258325446):
  both npm and Rust advisory jobs succeeded.
- New Windows NSIS installer built with the checked-in lockfiles. Archive
  integrity, installer/payload version 3.15.2, and payload x64 architecture passed.
  Silent installation exited 0; installed executable SHA-256 equals the extracted
  installer payload. The installed application starts successfully.
- Installed Windows ima: GLM-5.2 activation and automatic restart passed; read-only
  diagnostics confirmed both entry points selected the managed model with no
  pending transaction. The provider test verified ordinary responses, streaming,
  and tool calling using the updated TLS stack.
- Subsequent DeepSeek switching did not complete. The opted-in real-account
  roundtrip test received `modify_model` API code `100003` (`ima_rate_limited`).
  **This roundtrip test failed and remains a publication gate**, not a passed
  test or an approved exception. Do not repeatedly retry during rate limiting.
- Failure recovery reported `IMA_LIVE_RESTORATION=verified`. A separate read-only
  check confirmed both scene selections exactly match their pre-takeover
  baselines and every pending-transaction flag is false. The installed UI shows
  the original models in use. Existing user model rows are preserved.

The former Windows and Mac candidate hashes must not be reused for release.
Website metadata, release notes, checksums, and the previously prepared deployment
archive still describe superseded candidates. Regenerate that complete set only
after the replacement packages have passed verification; do not deploy the old
archive.

The user will build the Mac package on another computer after receiving the
fixed source commit. Public deployment and the release tag remain pending until
both replacement packages have passed validation.

See [Mac rebuild handoff](v3.15.2-macos-rebuild.md). The remaining real-account
Windows roundtrip must also pass after the service rate limit clears.
